07 / A TIME MACHINE WITH NO STEAM REQUIRED

Ada's time machine.

Choose a year. History has a source. Our Ada has an opinion.

We invented the following comments. They are not authentic quotations from Ada Lovelace.

1815● HISTORICAL BASIS

Hello, Ada.

Augusta Ada Byron, later known as Ada Lovelace, was born in 1815. Her parents were Annabella Milbanke and the poet Lord Byron.

What might Ada say about this today?

I brought a new kind of poetry into the family. No syntax yet, but exceptionally loud error notifications.

1833● HISTORICAL BASIS

The meeting that changed the brief.

Seventeen-year-old Ada met Charles Babbage and saw a demonstration of part of his calculating machine. This began a connection that later developed into a collaboration.

Check the historical source ↗
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

What might Ada say about this today?

I went to a party. I left with a long-term project and absolutely no estimate for hardware delivery.

1840 - 1841● HISTORICAL BASIS

Mathematics by post.

In 1840 and 1841, Ada studied advanced mathematics through correspondence with Augustus De Morgan. Their surviving letters document her learning and her questions.

Check the historical source ↗
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

What might Ada say about this today?

My online course had a latency of several days. Still, nobody ever said: can you hear me?

1843● HISTORICAL BASIS

Notes that outgrew the margins.

Her English translation of Menabrea's article on the Analytical Engine was published with extensive notes. Note G contains a procedure for calculating Bernoulli numbers.

Check the historical source ↗
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

What might Ada say about this today?

I only added a few comments. The reviewer ordered another teapot as a precaution.

1852● HISTORICAL BASIS

A life ends. A legacy continues.

Ada Lovelace died in 1852. Her published notes remained part of computing history and later discussions about what computers could do.

Check the historical source ↗
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

What might Ada say about this today?

A message for future teams: write documentation that can outlive the project's original author.

1983● HISTORICAL BASIS

Her name gets a compiler.

The first standard for the Ada programming language was published in 1983. The language honours her legacy with its name; she neither created nor used it herself.

Check the historical source ↗
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

What might Ada say about this today?

At last, they named something after me. I do hope the error messages have good manners.
